title: High-accuracy mini-stereotactic devices for minimally invasive middle and inner ear access
summary: The OtoJig System is used to create a small drill channel to access the middle and/or inner ear. The conCIerge software is used to plan the minimally invasive access route. It is also used to design the individually customized drilling guide, which specifies the direction toward the cochlea and the precise drilling depth and guides the surgical drills accurately. The diameter of the minimally invasive drill hole is approximately 0.13 to 4.5 mm, in graduated steps. In contrast, conventional cochlear implantation requires drilling away an area of bone approximately 30 to 50 mm in size behind the ear.

interventions.name: After voluntary informed consent has been obtained and screening has confirmed that access planning to the cochlea using the OtoJig software was successful, each study participant will undergo the minimally invasive procedure using the investigational devices. criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
• Adult Subjects (≥18 years)
• Subjects who are eligible to receive a MED-EL SYNCHRONY2 FLEX28 SL S-Vector cochlear implant according to the manufacturers IFU and the implanting centre
• OtoJig procedure deemed possible according to the surgeon based on imaging data from clinical CBCT imaging
• Signed informed consent to participate in the study and to allow for the evaluation of personal data.
Exclusion criteria:
• Subjects receiving a CI revision/reimplantation surgery (removal or replacement of a cochlear implant).
• Incapacitated subjects
• Subjects who received a previous ipsilateral mastoidectomy.
• Subjects with cholesteatoma in the surgical area of the planned access tunnel.
• Evidence of cochlear malformations or abnormal anatomy of the area of surgery deemed incompatible with the procedure by the surgeon.
• Evidence of acute or ongoing chronic middle ear or mastoid infections.
• Patients with bone disease in the area of surgery,
• Patients with infection in the area of surgery,
• Known or suspected sensitivity or allergies to:
- Titanium alloy
- Polyether ether ketone (PEEK),
- Polypropylene (PP)
- Chromium stainless steels
- Polyimide
• Quantitatively and/or qualitatively insufficient hard and/or soft tissue 
• Subjects where the planned access tunnel may intersect the segmentations of the facial nerve canal or the wall of the outer ear canal.
• Subjects for whom either no computed tomography volume image could be acquired due to medical reasons, the subject’s computed tomography volume image is of insufficient quality (including movement of the patient during acquisition) or other reasons which prevents surgeons from clearly identifying the boundaries of the anatomical structures.
• Participation in other (pharmacological) clinical trials within four weeks prior to enrolment
• Anything that, in the opinion of the Investigator, would 
- place the subject at increased risk 
- preclude the subject’s full compliance with the study or completion of the study
